passMeaning: Every pre-registered criterion is met except the recorded misses, which are reproduced exactly; every follow-up criterion is met; every failure control is rejected.
scope: Actual grains.js (derive, makeSim, forces, contact, wall, step, network and the instance settle) run headless in Node with the engine util and makeRng. Binary normal collisions (r0-r0, rmin-rmin and rmin-rmax pairs and a disk on the floor) at damping 0.05 to 0.9, refined from the production step to 1/64 of it; hardness 800, 4000, 12000; a disk sliding into rolling on the floor (friction 0.1, 0.4, 0.8); a disk on an incline at tan(theta)/3mu = 0.8, 0.95, 1.05, 1.25 (friction 0.2, 0.4, 0.8); an oblique grain-grain collision in gross sliding; the seven presets at seed cundall-1979 through the production settle, plus the pour geometry without friction; coordination at the pour geometry for friction 0, 0.4 and 0.8 over four seeds.

limitations: Contact-law benchmarks isolate one or two disks through a hand-built D (gravity and drag off for collisions); the packings are checked for static equilibrium and bookkeeping, not for their force distribution.

The settle is not a time-accurate collision integrator at its production step: the restitution coefficient depends on where in a step contact begins, from -12.1% to 5.7% of the analytic value at damping <= 0.5 (-25.3% to 7.4% up to 0.9). The pre-registered 10% bound was missed; the error converges at first order and is below 0.4% at h/64 for every phase.

The tangential spring is undamped and has finite stiffness, so a disk that starts sliding from rest overshoots the rigid Coulomb slip by an amount that scales as 1/sqrt(k_n) (8.7% at tan(theta)/3mu = 1.05 and hardness 4000); sustained sliding matches mu F_n to 1.4e-4. The pre-registered 3% bound on total slip was missed.

The starting lattice is not loose: 255 to 562 pairs overlap at the start, by up to 1.29 r0, and launch grains at up to 59 times the seeded kick speed, so each packing is prepared by an explosive decompression followed by settling, not a gentle pour.

The top load does not load the packing. At photo (press 0.03), strong (press 0.04), slip (press 0.03) the gravity settle is cut at half the step budget with kinetic energy 3.1e-4, 3.3e-2, 1.3e-2 per grain, far above the settle target, and the lid travels a strain of the top of a pile that is still compacting; it carries at most 3.4% of the weight at any step and nothing at the end. Presets with a top load are outside the validated domain.
The displayed equation of motion omits the background drag -c m v and -c I omega (c = zeta sqrt(g / r0) / 2) that grains.js applies to every grain; it does not enter the static balance.

The static load balance follows from Newton's third law once the packing is at rest; it certifies that the plate's network is a static one, not the statistics of force chains. Wall friction is history dependent (the arch preset's walls hold the pile down).

Seven presets at one seed and four seeds per friction value for Z; no all-parameter, Radjai force-distribution, Janssen-constant or experimental claim. The strongest-10% share mixes force-chain heterogeneity with the hydrostatic gradient and is recomputed, not interpreted.
